cross_product_finding: This page is the batch's purest example of the 'genuinely SDK-specific, needs its own vocabulary' side of the central question, with zero ambiguity: every setting here (TLS/security config, I/O pooling, circuit breakers, timeouts per-service, compression, retry strategy, JSON serializer, tracer, scheduler, event bus, connection-string parameters, system properties, configuration profiles) governs the BEHAVIOR OF THE CLIENT PROCESS, not any server-side statement or operation. None of it is 'the same underlying operation' as anything documented in server/'s or cloud/'s N1QL statement pages - a `queryTimeout` setting is a client-side concern layered on top of whichever statement eventually gets sent, but the setting itself has no server/-side statement counterpart to reuse. This confirms the batch instructions' own framing almost exactly ('connection management, error-handling/retry behavior, observability/tracing - these are properties of the client library... and probably need their own vocabulary') - no judgment call was really needed here, just consistent application of the sdk: namespace.
